> Purpose Uncertainty is inherent to clinical practice and impacts diagnostic reasoning, patient safety, and trust. Despite its ubiquity, health professions education has not adequately prepared learners to communicate uncertainty to patients, families, and care teams. Training remains variable and unevenly assessed. The authors examined how uncertainty communication is taught and assessed across the health professions and identified gaps to inform curricular development and scholarship. Method The authors conducted a scoping review guided by Arksey and O'Malley's framework and reported according to PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Eligible studies included learners from any health profession and addressed communication of uncertainty with patients and/or clinicians. Commentaries and reviews were excluded. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Ovid MEDLINE, Scopus, ERIC, CINAHL, and MedEdPORTAL beginning in March 2024 through August 2026. Data were analyzed using inductive and deductive analysis informed by Han's uncertainty taxonomy. Study quality was assessed using the Medical Education Research Study Quality Instrument (MERSQI). Furthermore, this paper aims to analyze the role of digital biomarkers in future decision-making. A structural characteristic of the DAS28 index is that its subjective components carry twice the weight of objective metrics. In cases of central sensitization, depression, or anxiety, this can result in "false-positive" disease activity, leading to unjustified and costly interventions, as well as ineffective therapy. Literature confirms that patient-physician discordance is one of the primary predictors of therapeutic failure, particularly in difficult-to-treat (D2T) cases. > Artificial intelligence (AI) is being investigated across the acute coronary syndrome (ACS) care pathway, including early diagnosis, coronary lesion characterization, procedural guidance, and risk prediction. This comprehensive review examines the current evidence across the entire ACS trajectory, with particular emphasis on clinically actionable and interventional applications. AI-enabled electrocardiography (ECG) may improve detection of myocardial infarction, including occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) that does not meet conventional STEMI criteria. Models combining clinical data and high-sensitivity troponin may improve early rule-out and rule-in. In coronary imaging, AI can quantify plaque characteristics and assist with the interpretation of OCT and IVUS, while image-derived physiology may help assess non-culprit lesions. However, better diagnostic accuracy does not necessarily translate into better revascularization decisions. AI-based models can also estimate post-ACS ischemic, bleeding, and mortality risk, although evidence that their use improves treatment or outcomes remains limited. > We report the case of a 34-year-old male with persistent fever, ascites, thrombocytosis and clinical deterioration despite broad-spectrum therapy who was ultimately diagnosed with peritoneal tuberculosis and concurrent chronic myeloid leukaemia. Initial investigations, including interferon-γ release assay and ascitic acid-fast bacilli, were negative, highlighting the limited sensitivity of traditional testing in extrapulmonary disease. Diagnosis required molecular testing and adenosine deaminase measurement, with delayed confirmation by culture. Bone marrow aspirate and trephine, pursued to broaden the differential diagnosis, revealed a Philadelphia chromosome. This case underscores the need for sustained diagnostic vigilance, multimodal investigation and avoidance of diagnostic parsimony.

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Athletes exposed to repetitive head impacts (RHI) may seek clinical evaluation because of concerns about chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a neuropathologically defined disease that cannot currently be diagnosed during life. As public awareness of CTE has expanded, clinicians face challenges communicating diagnostic uncertainty, interpreting non-specific symptoms, and addressing concerns about future neurological health. This Current Opinion examines the widening gap between public expectations and scientific capability and considers its implications for athlete-centered care. We discuss how clinicians can acknowledge uncertainty without dismissing patients' concerns, identify potentially treatable contributors to symptoms without prematurely attributing them to neurodegenerative disease, and use shared decision-making to guide individualized evaluation and management. We also consider how concerns about CTE may influence decisions about continued participation and return-to-sport among current athletes. Meeting these challenges requires coordinated interdisciplinary care, evidence-based communication, and clinical approaches that prioritize meaningful intervention even when...

PubMed, Scopus, CINAHL, Clinical Key, ProQuest, Research Gate and Science Direct were scanned to identify relevant studies. MeSH terms (prevalence, musculoskeletal, back pain, neck pain, posture, university students, and online education) and Boolean operators (OR and AND) were also used for search strategy. Only cross-sectional studies published between 2021 and 2025 were included in this review. The extracted data included author's name, year of publication, country of origin, sample size, field of study, tool for MSDs, affected body parts, and prevalence period. A total of 2254 records were identified, out of which 2232 were excluded, and only 22 were included for analysis. All included studies reported that the prevalence of MSP was consistently high among university students. The most common sites of pain were the neck, shoulder, and lower back. Musculoskeletal pain is highly prevalent among university students, which clearly indicates that there is an immediate requirement for specific preventive measures and ergonomic awareness programs for this population.

However, existing LLM-powered approaches do not account for the fact that effective scoring requires both holistic understanding of records and locally consistent judgments across similar ones. We present Attune, a mixed-initiative system for steerable LLM-powered scoring. Given a task description and scoring range, Attune performs pairwise comparisons across records to develop a global understanding first, and then resolves these comparisons into consistent score assignments—deriving scoring criteria and rules bottom-up in the process. These serve as shared representations of scoring logic that users can inspect and edit. Based on insights from a formative study (n = 12), Attune’s interface introduces novel steering interactions that allow users to deterministically refine scoring logic. > Three-dimensional Anatomy software is increasingly used in medical education, particularly for complex spatial topics such as Neuroanatomy and Head-Neck Anatomy. This study explored Anatomy educators’ perceptions regarding the effectiveness of 3D Anatomy software in teaching-learning these subjects. In qualitative study, used in-depth interviews with Anatomy educators who were also medical educationists. Interview data were analyzed thematically, and one major theme, “Perceived effectiveness of 3D Anatomy software,” was developed with three subthemes. Educators perceived the software as effective because it saved time, supported repeated visualization without damaging specimens, was most useful after students had acquired basic anatomical knowledge, and could potentially be incorporated into practical assessments. They viewed it as especially helpful in revision, higher-phase teaching, postgraduate education, and skill-based OSPE-style tasks. Anatomy educators considered 3D Anatomy software a valuable adjunct for advanced teaching, revision, and structured assessment, especially in anatomically complex regions.

> Abstract Background Physicians increasingly use artificial intelligence tools to support clinical work, yet there is no accepted standard for measuring the competency of large language models (LLMs) in clinical decision support. We developed EM-BENCH, a physician-validated, deterministically scored benchmark for evaluating whether models reliably apply the American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP) guidelines to clinical decisions. Methods EM-BENCH comprises 210 binary clinical vignettes covering all 70 critical questions across 25 ACEP clinical policies. We evaluated 149 LLM configurations representing 79 base models using prespecified answers and deterministic scoring. Each vignette had a prespecified correct answer to a binary yes-or-no question based on an ACEP recommendation. We examined associations between accuracy and model access tier (closed-access vs. open-weight models), model size, release date, clinical policy, recommendation evidence level, and reasoning settings. Today, digital delivery technologies have enabled broader reach than ever before. Yet these same technologies are often blamed for weakening the human connection essential for effective learning. This brief report describes how the small-group, live-virtual formats ECHO and Gather-ed use video conference technology (eg, Zoom) not merely as a distribution channel but as a deliberate architecture for interactivity, peer exchange, and sustained mentorship between learners and subject matter experts. Drawing on Project ECHO’s hub-and-spoke, case-based “all teach, all learn” philosophy and Gather-Ed’s facilitated peer-based social learning model, our experience, as illustrated in the report, demonstrates that structured small-group virtual learning reconciles the scalability demanded by modern continuing professional development with the relational engagement that participants and patients ultimately need.

**Mots-clés détectés :**

**Résumé / abstract :**

> The durability and stability of the cervical joint system of the KPSIT C50 crash dummy were evaluated. The two-element neck module has two degrees of freedom, enabling flexion-extension and right-left rotation. Drag torque characteristics were measured on a test bench using the point method, combining force and angular deflection measurements and compared with the Hybrid III reference dummy in the usable range. Durability was assessed in 200 crash tests over 24 months, with drag torque checked every 25 tests. No major parameter changes were found up to 75 tests. From about 100 tests, drag torque gradually decreased, mainly in the extreme motion zones. After 200 tests, the maximum reduction reached about 15% in flexion-extension and about 12% and 10% in rotation, while values in the central range remained stable. A 20 km/h frontal collision test showed larger head displacements after the program, indicating moderate growth in cervical compliance without loss of repeatability. The results confirm suitability for low-spin tests and support periodic torque checks after about 100 crashes.

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Primary pyruvate dehydrogenase complex deficiency (PDCD) comprises a group of monogenic disorders caused by pathogenic variants in genes encoding subunits of, or regulatory components affecting, the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex. The clinical phenotype spans a broad continuum, ranging from early onset congenital lactic acidosis to infantile or childhood onset global developmental delay with epilepsy, through to more attenuated adult-onset neurological presentations. Reports from patients and advocacy groups indicate substantial variability in clinical management across both emergency and outpatient settings and between centres internationally. Sensory processing depends on the integrity of neural systems and is essential to support lower-order functions as well as higher-order cognitive functions. Numerous studies have shown sensory patterns in autism correlate with social-communication and language skills across childhood. > CPR training requires learners to not only understand explicit procedural targets, such as compression depth and rate, but also to internalize these targets as stable psychomotor skills. However, existing CPR training systems often rely on feedback presented outside the action space, which divides learners’ attention between performing compressions and monitoring external guidance. This separation weakens the coupling between action and bodily sensation and may lead to an over-reliance on external feedback, compromising skill retention once support is removed. To address this challenge, we conducted a formative study with novice trainees and certified BLS instructors, from which we derived three design goals: embedding feedback within the task space, providing active kinesthetic guidance, and gradually fading assistance based on learning phases. Informed by these insights, we designed Kinesthetic-CPR, a stage-adaptive multimodal mixed reality CPR training system, and evaluated it in a controlled user study across two sub-studies (N = 60). This work offers design implications for CPR training systems that aim to better support skill retention.

**Résumé / abstract :**

> In the absence of guidelines from professional societies, periprocedural fasting practices in enteral nutrition vary widely and often lead to preventable, clinically significant nutritional deficits. To address the heterogeneity of current clinical practice, the authors aimed to develop expert consensus on best practices for the periprocedural management of tube feeding using a modified Delphi consensus process. Draft recommendations were iteratively modified during a four-round Delphi process by a multidisciplinary international panel of experts. After iterative consolidation and modification, a total of 20 recommendations were produced by round 4, and all recommendations achieved stability. Final recommendations advocate for the protocolization of institutional perioperative fasting approaches and establish best practices for perioperative management of tube feeding in patients with and without a secure airway (cuffed endotracheal or cuffed tracheostomy tube) across a range of common clinical scenarios. The recommendations are intended to harmonize local practices internationally and safely minimize unnecessary periprocedural nutritional loss.

### A metacognitive approach to learning and performance in human-AI interaction

- **Auteurs** : Yizhou Fan, Lixiang Yan, Inge Molenaar, Samuel Greiff, Dragan Gašević

**Mots-clés détectés :**

  - **ai_anchor** : artificial intelligence

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly becoming a pervasive technology across education, work, research, and everyday life. Yet growing evidence suggests that fluent, coherent, and seemingly transparent AI assistance can improve task performance while weakening the metacognitive engagement and deeper processing required for durable learning. This tension raises a central question about how does offloading to AI reshape human learning, and under what conditions do performance and learning decouple? In this Perspective, we introduce the Synergetic Notion of Human-AI Skills and Knowledge Construction (SYNC) model. The model offers a metacognitive account of human-AI interaction by conceptualising metacognitive offloading and metacognitive onloading. The SYNC model aims to explain how human-AI interaction unfolds across learning and performance dimensions, clarifying how learners may drift into overreliant AI-supported performance or move toward human-AI synergy. We further identify key pitfalls in ineffective human-AI interaction and outline strategies to address them through metacognitive onloading and support human-AI synergy.

> Amateur badminton players increasingly record matches, yet existing tools provide only aggregate statistics or generic summaries, leaving most unable to extract tactical insights without expert guidance. A formative study (N=8) reveals the need for multi-granularity, video-anchored tactical analysis centered on rallies. We derive a taxonomy of performance issues from national-level athletes’ annotations and present TactiPlay, an interactive system that instantiates an expert-taxonomy-guided, rally-level, video-anchored review workflow. The system’s analytical pipeline organizes match events into taxonomy-grounded feedback, while its interface links structured reports to rally summaries, video evidence, and court visualizations. A within-subjects study (N=16) shows that TactiPlay elicits more frequent, concrete, actionable, and appropriate reflections than a report-and-statistics baseline. These findings show how organizing reviewed match evidence into a taxonomy-guided, video-linked workflow can support amateur players’ tactical reflection.

> PURPOSE: Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy (DCM) is the most common form of atraumatic spinal cord compression. Few population estimates have been reported, with most estimates derived from hospital records. The aim was to estimate the incidence of DCM in UK primary care. METHODS: Population cohort study using the Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD) Aurum database of English general practices, restricted to adults aged 20 years and over, 2013-2023. Incidence was calculated as new DCM diagnoses per calendar year divided by the registered adult population at each year's midpoint, reported per 100,000 person-years with 95% CIs, crude and age-standardised (AS), by gender and age band. > Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is a major cause of low back pain, driven largely by nucleus pulposus cell (NPC) senescence under chronic hypoxia and nutrient stress. Serine metabolism regulates senescence, but its role in IVDD remains unclear. Here, transcriptomic profiling reveals that the glycine-serine-threonine pathway is downregulated in senescent NPCs, with marked reduction of the serine synthesis rate limiting enzyme PHGDH. This is confirmed by single cell RNA sequencing of human discs, aged rat tissues, and degenerated human samples, accompanied by decreased intracellular serine. PHGDH silencing or serine deprivation inhibits NPC proliferation, induces senescence, and suppresses matrix anabolism. Mechanistically, PHGDH deficiency lowers α ketoglutarate, impairing histone demethylation and increasing H3K27me3 occupancy at the Rap1b promoter, which silences Rap1b and activates mTORC1, thereby blocking autophagic flux. Additionally, serine starvation depletes glutathione, elevates ROS, and promotes apoptosis. > Medical education transmits more than formal knowledge; it signals what matters through formal, informal, and hidden curricula. Drawing on Schein's theory of organizational culture, this commentary synthesizes insights from three 2026 Research in Medical Education studies to examine how artifacts, values, and underlying assumptions shape learning environments. The reviewed studies-on multimorbidity in undergraduate medical education, ritualized group handoff in residency, and learner recovery from failure-illustrate how educational practices encode organizational priorities in distinct ways. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Prehospital damage-control amputation in civilian emergency systems is rare, especially combined with prehospital packed red blood cell transfusion. We report a 30-year-old man with bilateral lower-limb crush injury after entrapment in an industrial roller machine in a remote area. Despite initially preserved blood pressure, he developed marked hemodynamic deterioration and arrived at the hospital with a blood pressure of 74/49 mmHg. Both limbs were non-salvageable. Prehospital bilateral amputation with vascular ligation was performed on scene, followed by transfusion of one local unit of packed red blood cells (~200 ml). He survived after stump revision, intensive care, and rehabilitation. This case describes the sequential use of prehospital hemorrhage control and packed red blood cell transfusion during the same prehospital episode in a patient with a life-threatening entrapment injury and delayed transport.

### Unlocking the Potential of Cardiac Rehabilitation: From Psychological Barriers to Treatment Targets.

- **Auteurs** : Hafkamp F, Hermans H, Kupper N.
- **Revue** :

- **Tags proposés** : Aucun tag proposé

**Mots-clés détectés :**

  - **physio_anchor** : rehabilitation

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Purpose of review To provide an overview of the dual role of psychological factors: as determinants of cardiac rehabilitation (CR) engagement and long-term behavior change, and as consequences and treatment targets. Recent findings CR is central to cardiovascular care but remains underused. Beyond systemic and logistical barriers, psychological factors influence whether patients participate in and complete CR and maintain a healthy lifestyle post-CR. Psychological distress is common in patients eligible for CR and negatively affects quality of life and prognosis. Without addressing these factors, CR jeopardizes remaining an effective but underused intervention which full potential is not realized. Psychological factors should be understood both as barriers to CR participation, completion, and long-term benefit, and as actionable targets to improve these outcomes. They should therefore not be limited to intake risk screening but assessed and acted upon across the CR pathway to support engagement and enhance sustained behavior change and patient-centered recovery.

> Patients with chronic pain often experience behavioral issues linked to pain, depression, and other emotional disorders. These problems stem from dysfunction in the mesocorticolimbic system, and exercise offers a safe, accessible, and effective alternative. It not only reduces pain but also activates multiple neural pathways, helping restore normal function. First, in the periphery, exercise promotes the release of myokines, which are essential for the body-brain connection and influence neural activity. IGF-1, released from muscles during exercise, can cross the blood-brain barrier and affect the brain. IGF-1 specifically targets orexin neurons in the hypothalamus, which then stimulate dopamine neurons in the ventral tegmental area, triggering the reward system. Second, exercise can reshape neural circuits and restore mesocorticolimbic function, reducing chronic pain and related issues. We showed that exercise activates neurons in the basal nucleus of the amygdala that project to the nucleus accumbens, supporting patients' goal-directed behavior. Early Platforms and Water Flood constitute the earlier Urabarroid aggregate; Stone Rooms, Midden, and Late Platforms constitute the later Janabarroid aggregate. Methods We systematically searched Apple Podcasts and Spotify using specialty-specific terms and manually reviewed the top twenty journals in the field for affiliated podcasts. Included were active, English-language, physician-hosted podcasts. Results Eighty-five podcasts (53.0% US-based) comprising 10,190 episodes were analyzed. > Entrapment neuropathies are the most prevalent focal neuropathic pain conditions globally and impose a substantial individual and socioeconomic burden. Traditionally conceptualised as purely mechanical compression syndromes, this view is increasingly challenged by converging evidence from human tissue analyses, advanced neuroimaging, and deep clinical phenotyping. Entrapment neuropathies are now recognised as biologically dynamic disorders shaped to different extents by microvascular compromise, demyelination, axonal degeneration, immune dysregulation, neuroinflammation, central nervous system adaptations, and psychosocial influences. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Background: A digital book may support learning instrument names and functions, but knowledge scores do not establish practical competence. Objective: To compare immediate posttest instrument knowledge between INSTADAN and lecturer PowerPoint groups after baseline adjustment. Methods: This nonrandomized study analyzed 161 first year midwifery students from four intact classes (INSTADAN, n=78; control, n=83). A 30 item knowledge test was administered before and after teaching. Individual level ANCOVA adjusted for pretest score, age, and information sources with HC3 standard errors. Results: Mean scores rose from 68.72 to 85.04 with INSTADAN and from 68.84 to 79.88 with PowerPoint. The adjusted difference was 6.08 points (95% CI, 3.99 to 8.17; P<0.001), equivalent to approximately 1.82 correct answers. Student stratified bootstrap gave a 95% interval of 4.05 to 8.14 points. Neither method adjusted for class dependence. Conclusion: INSTADAN was associated with higher immediate knowledge scores; four class allocation, baseline imbalance, and incomplete assessment documentation limit causal interpretation. Retention and practical competence were not examined.

Wearable technologies, which include inertial measurement units, surface electromyography sensors, smart textiles, photoplethysmography-based devices, pressure-sensing insoles and smart garments, now capture movement, muscle activity, physiological load and adherence data outside the clinic. When these data streams are interpreted by artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning and deep learning, they can be transformed into clinically meaningful information such as exercise quality, gait deviations, fall risk, fatigue, pain-related behaviour and recovery trajectories. > Upper-extremity injuries are common in tennis and are predominantly associated with repetitive mechanical loading. Modern professional tennis has evolved substantially, with greater topspin production, higher racquet-head speeds, prolonged baseline exchanges, increased physical demands, and dense competitive schedules. These changes may influence the cumulative mechanical environment experienced by the upper extremity. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence regarding elbow injury risk in tennis, with particular attention to workload, stroke biomechanics, fatigue, kinetic-chain function, recovery capacity, and tennis ball characteristics. The available literature supports a multifactorial perspective in which stroke volume, stroke intensity, topspin demand, fatigue accumulation, and equipment-related factors may interact to influence cumulative mechanical exposure, while recovery capacity and kinetic-chain efficiency may modify the athlete’s ability to tolerate and adapt to repeated loading. > Purpose Alzheimer's disease is a leading cause of disability among older adults and poses increasing challenges for healthcare systems. In Denmark, demographic changes and healthcare reform are driving greater involvement of primary care in diagnosis and management. Materials and methods This paper examines the rationale for a general practice-centred model and summarises recent diagnostic developments, including blood-based biomarkers. Results Although current disease-modifying therapies show only modest benefit, ongoing research and scalable biomarkers enable earlier and more accessible diagnosis. We propose a pragmatic three-step diagnostic approach for primary care, with structured clinical and cognitive assessment, exclusion of secondary causes including structural neuroimaging, and in the near future, the availability of feasible biomarkers to support diagnosis and guide referral. We also outline key organisational, educational and ethical requirements for implementation. Conclusion A general practice-centred model may improve diagnostic timeliness, accessibility and continuity of care if integrated within a robust clinical and ethical framework.

> Fat embolism syndrome (FES) is a rare, life-threatening complication of sickle cell disease (SCD), often underrecognized due to overlap with acute chest syndrome, sepsis, and thrombotic microangiopathies. We report a 37-year-old man with sickle cell disease who presented with an acute vaso-occlusive crisis and rapidly deteriorated with respiratory failure, cardiovascular collapse, and neurological dysfunction. Common etiologies including pulmonary embolism, infection, and stroke were excluded. Laboratory evidence of hemolysis, cytopenias, elevated ferritin, and acute cor pulmonale suggested systemic FES secondary to bone marrow necrosis. The patient underwent urgent red cell exchange transfusion, followed by therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids, resulting in significant clinical and hemodynamic recovery. This case highlights the importance of early recognition and aggressive multimodal therapy in SCD-FES.

Results The results showed that, in general, participants who were more susceptible to misinformation held right-wing, populist, and conspiracist worldviews, as well as a low need for cognition and a low need for closure. > This edited volume examines the concept of maturity ("Mündigkeit/Myndighed") as a central educational aim within the context of school and teacher education. Particularly drawing on Adorno's critical theory, maturity is understood here not only as a cognitive attribute but as a relational and political process. Contributions from various disciplines illuminate historical aspects, theoretical perspectives, and practical experiences to highlight maturity as a guiding principle of pedagogical practice. Current societal challenges such as digitalization, political polarization, and authoritarian structures are addressed alongside the role of teachers in fostering critical thinking and solidarity. The volume is based on a two-year German-Scandinavian research dialogue coordinated by the Heidelberg School of Education. Its aim is to provide impulses for a teacher education that empowers individuals toward self-determination and responsible action.

> Non-ossifying fibromas (NOFs) are usually seen in growing children and are often found incidentally. Their presence in adults, particularly when associated with pain, is highly uncommon and can lead to diagnostic uncertainty. This case report describes a 27-year-old female presenting with persistent pain in the right proximal part of the leg for 2 years. Despite conservative treatment, including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and zoledronic acid, the pain remained unresolved. Imaging revealed a small, eccentric, lytic lesion suggestive of an NOF, which was confirmed by histopathological examination. The patient underwent curettage and bone grafting with significant postoperative pain relief in proximal tibial metaphysis. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of symptomatic NOFs in adults and emphasizes integrating clinical, radiological, and histological findings to arrive at an accurate diagnosis. Surgical intervention, although uncommon, can be considered in symptomatic cases and may yield excellent outcomes.

This article presents the first major empirical study focusing on the directionality of pharmaceuticalisation by taking cost-effectiveness assessment and regulation of anticoagulants in England by the National Institute of Health and Care Excellence (NICE) as a case study. During this century, anticoagulant therapy for the prevention of stroke and systemic embolism has changed direction profoundly away from warfarin towards newer and markedly more expensive direct oral anticoagulants. > Background: Entrusting clinical responsibility to a trainee is both an everyday occurrence and a high-stakes judgment in clinical education. Knowledge of entrustment decision-making has developed primarily within medical education. Postgraduate nursing education, a predominantly practice-based system in which registered nurses train for specialized clinical roles, has remained largely unexplored. Moreover, preceptors regularly struggle to articulate their judgments, including intuitive impressions that are difficult to put into words. Aim: To unravel entrustment decision-making by preceptors in Dutch postgraduate nursing education. Methods: Four complementary studies were conducted. A qualitative interview study with 16 preceptors from acute care, pediatrics, and oncology explored the considerations underlying entrustment decisions. A conceptual study proposed a model to distinguish legitimate subjectivity from unwanted bias. An exploratory sequential mixed-methods study, combining three focus groups (n=19) with a two-round Delphi procedure (n=29 and n=23), identified essential trainee characteristics. Finally, a proof-of-concept case study with an action research design evaluated...

> BACKGROUND: Firearm injuries remain a leading cause of preventable death in the United States (US), with physicians uniquely positioned to contribute to firearm injury prevention (FIP). Despite this, there is a lack of recent national assessment of FIP inclusion in US undergraduate medical education (UME). Thus, we looked to assess how medical schools currently incorporate FIP into curricula and what challenges affect its implementation. METHODS: We distributed a REDCap-based survey to medical education leadership at all LCME- and COCA- accredited medical schools in the US between April and December 2024, assessing FIP curricular content, timing, modes and settings of instruction, assessment strategies, extracurricular opportunities, and perceived barriers to implementation. RESULTS: Fifty-five institutions (27%) responded, with 64% reporting the inclusion of FIP content in their curricula. Most schools (62%) introduced FIP during clinical years, particularly in pediatrics, emergency medicine, and surgery, and some schools (51%) integrated content preclinically. This systematic review aimed to analyze the available empirical evidence on the incorporation of interculturality into the curricula of university health science programs, in order to identify the main strengths, weaknesses, and training gaps reported in the literature, as well as the pedagogical and curricular strategies proposed to strengthen and implement it. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Advances in acute burn care have improved survival, shifting focus toward long-term functional recovery. Facial burns present a distinct clinical challenge due to the concentration of ocular, oral, respiratory, and expressive functions within a highly visible anatomical region. This narrative review synthesises functional and psychosocial literature to examine facial burns as trauma that disrupts dynamic facial movement, communication, and participation, and to evaluate limitations in current outcome frameworks. The face supports ocular protection, articulation, alimentation, airway patency, and non-verbal signalling. Contracture patterns, including microstomia, ectropion, nasal distortion, and midfacial contracture, may impair both mechanical function and expressive range. Recovery is typically longitudinal and iterative, addressing evolving distortion rather than restoring pre-injury dynamics. Even subtle restrictions of facial movement may alter speech clarity, eye contact, and self-recognition, with consequences extending beyond visible scarring. Existing outcome measures, including body image scales, burn-specific health instruments, and isolated physical metrics, do not adequ...

Treating the two as tracks of a single academic-development continuum, this article asks how each has been institutionalized and localized in Japan, and what constrains the translation of policy into teaching improvement. > This study aims to explore the physical-acoustic characteristics of talilo huidu bamboo from Bone Bolango, Tomini Bay area, in the production of Polopalo, while formulating geometric standards to preserve local ecology and cultural heritage. Utilizing a qualitative method as the primary approach, this research integrates oral ethnoorganological studies with sound analysis via Fast Fourier Transform in Audacity as supporting data, alongside the sound philosophy concepts of the Gorontalo community. The results successfully formulate precise geometric standards for the Polopalo blade: a base length of 154 mm and a wall thickness of 10–12 mm with a proportional resonator hole to maintain traditional sound accuracy. By integrating origin–destination matrices with spatial infrastructure topologies, the methodology calculates distinct exposure profiles. In Phase 1, six summary and six question prompts across two models were scored with 2,692 rubric annotations. Claude Prompt 0 produced the best summaries (composite 76.9%) and GPT Prompt 1 the best questions (79.6%); quality varied widely by prompt, and neither model won both tasks. **Résumé / abstract :**

> ABSTRACT Marine fish offer sustainable defense strategies to address the global challenge posed by rising temperatures, which threaten public health, accelerate material degradation, and intensify environmental stress. Through constant interaction with their aquatic environment, fish secrete a natural supramolecular protective mucus hydrogel, rich in gel‐forming glycoproteins (mucins), multiple antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), and ultraviolet‐protective mycosporine‐like amino acids (MAAs). This multifunctional protective system provides integrated physicochemical and biological protection against radiation, pathogens, and environmental material degradation. Inspired by this natural defensive mechanism, the sustainable recovery and engineering of fish mucus‐derived supramolecular hydrogels may provide an advanced sustainable system for the development of biobased technologies. In this framework, the perspective highlights how biomimetic replication of sustainable supramolecular hydrogels can be applied to support human health, mitigate marine environmental degradation, and contribute to achieving the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

> Phototherapy is a non-invasive therapeutic modality that uses specific wavelengths of light to modulate biological processes and treat disease. Driven by advances in photobiology, regenerative medicine, and clinical technology, phototherapy has evolved from empirical heliotherapy into a mechanism-based intervention with expanding medical applications. This review places the biological effects, therapeutic indications, and safety profiles of ultraviolet, blue, and green light in comparative context, while focusing primarily on the mechanisms, dosimetry, and clinical translation of red and near-infrared photobiomodulation (PBM). Although ultraviolet and blue light therapies have established roles in dermatology and neonatal jaundice, their clinical use is limited by concerns such as photocarcinogenesis, retinal phototoxicity, and circadian disruption. In contrast, red and near-infrared light offer deeper tissue penetration and, when appropriately dosed, a comparatively low risk of direct photochemical injury. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) offers a potential long term, corticosteroid-free, therapy for selected patients with facet-mediated spinal pain. This narrative review examines lumbar and cervical clinical studies and provides an expert perspective. Several comparative studies report pain and functional improvement, with some suggesting sustained lumbar benefit beyond that of corticosteroids. Cervical studies also show encouraging outcomes. However, recent randomized trials have not consistently demonstrated superiority, and preparation variability complicates interpretation. PRP merits continued clinical investigation and individualized consideration, with transparent counseling, image-guided delivery, and standardized outcome assessment. Symptomatic improvement should not be equated with proven joint regeneration.

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Background Placement of a subfascial drain following open spine surgery is common practice to mitigate postoperative complications, including epidural hematoma, seroma formation, surgical site infection, and wound dehiscence. The authors present 3 cases in which subfascial Hemovac drains were associated with postoperative durotomy following otherwise uncomplicated lumbar surgeries. Observations Three patients who underwent single-level lumbar surgery requiring postoperative drain placement subsequently developed CSF leaks, presumed to be secondary to intracorporeal drain movement consistent with the Euler buckling theory. Lessons In patients undergoing uncomplicated single-level lumbar spine surgery, consideration should be given to the use of a silicone Jackson-Pratt drain rather than a compression-resistant polyvinyl chloride Hemovac drain. In a small surgical bed, a shorter and more compliant drain may be sufficient, whereas a stiff drain may act as a trocar. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE2640.

> Gridhrasi is one among the Vataja Nanatmaja Vyadhis described in Ayurveda and is characterized predominantly by pain radiating from the Sphik region towards the Kati, Pristha, Uru, Janu, Jangha and Pada. The clinical presentation of Gridhrasi closely resembles sciatica in contemporary medicine, where pain commonly follows the distribution of the sciatic nerve. A 45 year old male patient presented with complaints of low back pain radiating to the Right lower limb since 2 months associated with stiffness and difficult to walk. clinical examination revealed tests positive. Based on ayurvedic clinical assessment, the case was diagnosed as Vataja Gridhrasi. This patient was managed with yoga basthi along with other bahya karmas, internal medication, physiotherapy and yogatherapy. Appropriate dietary and lifestyle advice was also provided. Following the first course of treatment, the patient demonstrated considerable relief from radiating pain and stiffness, along with improved functional mobility and the ability to perform daily activities more comfortably.

Adults aged 60 to 70 years carry a high burden of symptomatic disease and frequently have comorbidities that limit the long-term use of oral analgesics and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, which has stimulated interest in non-pharmacological physical agents. High-intensity electromagnetic stimulation devices, such as the Super Inductive System (SIS; BTL Industries), generate rapidly changing magnetic fields of up to 3 tesla that induce electric currents capable of depolarizing peripheral nerves and eliciting muscle contractions without skin contact. PBM using red and near-infrared light may enhance proper mitochondrial function by acting on cytochrome c oxidase (CCO) and other signaling pathways, including the transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) channel, leading to increased ATP production, modulation of ROS signaling, and improved cellular homeostasis. We review in vitro, animal, and clinical studies investigating PBM in metabolic, neurodegenerative, hepatic, cardiovascular, age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and skeletal muscle disorders associated with aging, as well as its application in the management of cancer therapy-related oral mucositis. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Calcified thoracic disc herniation is uncommon but carries substantial operative risk. A 67-year-old man with 12 months of progressive myelopathy from a T7-T8 disc herniation underwent posterior laminectomy and instrumented fusion without preoperative computed tomography (CT). He developed near-complete paraplegia, with lower-limb power of Medical Research Council grade 0-1/5. Subsequent CT demonstrated a densely calcified ventral disc. Following transfer, full-endoscopic transforaminal discectomy was performed to address the ventral compression without spinal cord retraction. By three months after the revision procedure, power improved to grade 4-4+/5 and he regained ambulation using a walking frame. Thoracic disc herniations being considered for surgery should be characterised with CT as well as magnetic resonance imaging. Calcified lesions warrant subspecialty review and an approach that directly addresses the ventral pathology. In selected patients, endoscopic discectomy may achieve effective decompression with limited access morbidity.

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Purulent–necrotic infections of the surgical wound following instrumented correction of thoracolumbar scoliosis remain among the most serious complications in spinal surgery, because they often require implant removal, prolonged disability, and recurrence. In adult patients undergoing surgery at a mature age for scoliosis deformity (traditionally corrected in childhood or adolescence), such complications occur less frequently and have specific clinical features. The presented clinical case of a 46-year-old patient with a postoperative wound infection in the form of purulent–necrotic phlegmon after correction of the thoracic spine illustrates successful preservation of spinal instrumentation after six revision and debridement procedures, followed by installation of a vacuum-assisted closure (VAC) system and two VAC system replacements with complete wound closure. This case suggests the potential value of repeated surgical debridement combined with vacuum-assisted therapy as an effective approach to implant salvage even in severe purulent-necrotic processes, which is of significant importance for clinical practice.

Comparison with the aardvark reveals alternative pathways of skeletal reinforcement, with ground pangolins showing relatively greater secondary remodelling in the hind limb. > Retroperitoneal sarcomas are rare, aggressive malignancies that often present late owing to the retroperitoneum's anatomical expansibility. Dedifferentiated liposarcoma is the most common high-grade subtype. We describe the technical management of a 65-year-old man with a giant retroperitoneal dedifferentiated liposarcoma involving multiple adjacent organs, treated by radical en bloc multivisceral resection including the kidney, adrenal gland, spleen, and distal pancreas. Postoperative recovery was complicated by a Grade B pancreatic leak and a left pleural effusion, managed with percutaneous and thoracic drainage, respectively. Histology confirmed a dedifferentiated liposarcoma resected with clear (R0) margins. At 18 months, no radiological recurrence had been observed, although this follow-up interval remains short relative to the recurrence interval reported for high-grade dedifferentiated liposarcoma. This case illustrates the technical conduct of multivisceral resection for a giant retroperitoneal sarcoma and the perioperative surveillance required to manage expected complications such as pancreatic leak.

> Atrioventricular conduction disturbances and the need for cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) therapy are frequently required after transcatheter tricuspid valve implantation (TTVI). The interaction between the annulus, transcatheter heart valve and the leads is often complex and the optimal management under debate. We prospectively included 36 patients undergoing TTVI between June 2021 and January 2025. 14 patients had a preexisting CIED. 11 patients experienced right ventricular lead-jailing without signs for early or delayed lead failure after one year, one patient underwent lead extraction and two patients had a leadless pacemaker. In four patients, a pacemaker in LBBAP was successfully implanted due to new-onset postoperative atrioventricular block. The device measurements as well as the valve function remained stable over a follow-up of at least one up to 2.5 years with persistent LBB-capture. This case series demonstrates that LBBAP following TTVI is feasible with encouraging early outcomes. Careful patient selection and dedicated follow-up are essential for patients with CIED treated with TTVI.

Pre‐existing OSA is found in about 60–75% of stroke survivors, yet up to 80–90% remain undiagnosed before hospitalization. OSA induces physiological stress through intermittent hypoxemia, oxidative injury, severe intrathoracic pressure swings, hypercoagulability, and autonomic instability. These pathways accelerate systemic atherosclerosis, promote atrial fibrillation, worsen acute stroke severity, double the risk of recurrent CVA, and increase all-cause mortality (RR 1.69). Yet despite extensive study, the pathogenesis of both remains incompletely understood, and neither has been associated with a genetic mutation. > Low back pain is viewed as a public health problem. Women have a higher prevalence of low back pain than men in all age groups. Pilates is currently one of the most popular exercise methods in the world, so the aim of this review paper is to cover and consolidate the existing literature that points to the use of Pilates in women diagnosed with low back pain. Web of Science, Scopus, and PubMed databases were used for the literature review. The inclusion criteria were: the study includes women as participants, the participants were diagnosed with low back pain, a specific Pilates method was used, the participants have no other diseases and are not pregnant, the study is written in English. Based on the database search, 108 papers were identified, of which nine met all criteria and were included in the final analysis. These studies covered 445 women, with 251 women undergoing a specific type of Pilates program. The results showed that Pilates programs influenced pain reduction, improvement of muscular and functional abilities, as well as improvement of quality of life. Therefore, Pilates can be a very good way to reduce low back pain, especially in the female population.

On examination, she had a tuft of hair in the midline of the low back. MRI of the whole spine revealed a lumbosacral intradural hematoma with incidental findings of spinal dysraphism-diastematomyelia and tethering of the spinal cord. > Extracellular vesicle therapies have been developed for tissue repair, but how donor-cell senescence reshapes vesicle-mediated mitochondrial transfer remains unclear. Here, we show that senescent adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs) redirect damaged mitochondria into microvesicles (MVs), converting protective vesicles into pro-degenerative carriers. Senescent ADSC-derived MVs are enriched in PINK1-marked, oxidatively damaged mitochondrial cargo. After transfer to nucleus pulposus cells (NPCs), this cargo disrupts recipient mitochondrial homeostasis, activates the cGAS-STING-NLRP3 inflammatory axis, and aggravates intervertebral disc degeneration. > Koala Retrovirus (KoRV) is in transition from exogenous virus to endogenous element and shows distinct profiles between northern and southern koala populations. Northern animals carry high proviral copy numbers of endogenous KoRV-A and a range of exogenous subtypes, while southern koalas instead generally only possess degraded and recombinant versions of the virus. In this study we investigated the KoRV profiles of koalas in the Snowy Monaro (SM) region of southern NSW, which is at the intersection between northern and southern populations. We found that SM koalas have lower KoRV loads and proviral copy numbers than koalas from other northern populations. Plasma RNA subtype profiles were very consistent between individuals with all animals having KoRV-A at low relative abundance and high proportions of subtypes D and L. This pattern of subtype profiles is unique compared to other populations studied and suggests that KoRV-D and/or L may be endogenous in southern NSW or that KoRV-A is effectively suppressed in koalas from the region. > Abstract A 10‐year‐old, spayed, female domestic shorthair cat was referred for acute inspiratory dyspnoea and stridor. Diagnostic tests, including endoscopy, computed tomography and cytology, showed a circumferential tracheal mass within the mid‐cervical trachea, compatible with an extramedullary plasmacytoma. The cat underwent tracheal resection (21% of the total length) and end‐to‐end anastomosis without perioperative complications. Postoperative recovery was uneventful, and the cat was discharged 3 days after surgery. At the 12‐month postoperative follow‐up, no recurrence of clinical signs was observed. The histopathological analysis revealed a plasmacytoma with no infiltration of the surgical margins. This case highlights the feasibility and outcome of surgical management of rare tracheal neoplasms in cats.

This narrative review summarizes its relationships with osteoporosis, sarcopenia, locomotive syndrome, and frailty. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched for English-language publications from database inception through December 31, 2025. Relevant evidence was reviewed narratively. Observational studies indicate that osteoporosis-associated vertebral fragility is an important structural contributor to kyphotic progression through clinically apparent or unrecognized vertebral fractures and progressive vertebral deformity. Degenerative disc changes and local trunk muscle dysfunction may also contribute through altered spinal loading and reduced active postural support. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Arthroscopic hip labral reconstruction has become an important tool for treating irreparable labral pathology, particularly in the revision setting. Restoration of the acetabular labrum is critical for hip stability, load distribution, and maintenance of the joint suction seal. Segmental labral reconstruction allows focal defects to be addressed while preserving healthy native labral tissue. This technical note describes a reproducible technique for segmental labral reconstruction using a peroneus longus allograft. The use of a peroneus longus allograft provides consistent graft sizing and avoids donor-site morbidity. This technique emphasizes a stepwise approach, including appropriate patient selection, portal placement, graft preparation, controlled graft delivery, and secure fixation to restore labral function and stability. Segmental reconstruction is particularly useful for focal irreparable defects and may help restore joint mechanics and the suction seal while avoiding unnecessary circumferential reconstruction.

> Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is a well-established oncogenic driver in multiple solid tumors, most prominently in breast and gastric cancers. Beyond gene amplification-driven signaling through canonical PI3K/AKT and RAS/MAPK pathways, emerging evidence reveals that HER2 functions within a highly dynamic and context-dependent tumor ecosystem. Interactions between HER2-positive tumor cells and immune and stromal compartments actively shape the tumor microenvironment, contributing to immune evasion, therapeutic resistance and disease progression. A central challenge in the clinical management of HER2-altered cancers is pronounced spatial and temporal heterogeneity, which undermines both diagnostic accuracy and the durability of targeted therapies. In response, advances in multi-omics profiling, liquid biopsy technologies and artificial intelligence-assisted analytics are redefining HER2 assessment, shifting it from static tissue-based classification towards dynamic, minimally invasive monitoring. Despite clear evidence supporting secondary fracture prevention, postfracture care often emphasizes the recovery from the injury itself while insufficiently addressing the underlying skeletal disease. As a result, approximately 6% of patients will have a subsequent fragility fracture within 1 year of the initial injury. In addition, without intervention, osteoporosis will progress in these patients resulting in chronic pain, disability, and decreased quality of life. > Most software systems are optimized for successful execution. Their primary question is: Can the requested action be performed? Governance systems, integrity systems, audit systems, provenance systems, and constitutional systems face a different question: Can an action be refused correctly, consistently, durably, and verifiably? This distinction is foundational. A conventional application often presents successful operation as evidence of trustworthiness. A governance system also requires principled refusal. Neither success nor refusal is sufficient by itself; each must be scoped, evidenced, and connected to observed effects. It must reject forged authority, corrupted records, invalid lineage, inconsistent state, replayed requests, malformed inputs, and unverifiable claims. Failure to refuse correctly is itself a governance failure. This paper proposes the Integrity Enforcement Layer (IEL), a constitutional substrate positioned beneath governance logic and above storage, execution, and transport mechanisms. The IEL centralizes adversarial validation, verification semantics, corruption handling, atomic mutation, and contextual reconstruction into a single enforcement spine. The purp...

> Dopaminergic replacement therapy via L-DOPA is the major medical therapy for Parkinsons Disease. Long-term L-DOPA administration is known to cause dyskinetic movements, L-DOPA Induced Dyskinesia (LID). It remains unclear if the LID related, maladaptive changes in brain structure/function are localized to neural circuits within the nigrostriatal DA system or have brainwide impact. We employed multi-shell diffusion magnetic resonance imaging and correlational tractography to investigate structural brain networks associated with daily administration of L-DOPA and the development of LID in the unilateral 6-hydroxydopamine rat model. 53% of rats receiving L-DOPA therapy developed severe LID. Tractography found brainwide statistical maps positively and negatively associated with LID severity highlighted by bilateral neural circuits contained in the lesioned nigrostriatal system as well as others including the cerebellum and prefrontal cortex. These results suggest that systemic dysfuntion in brainwide neural circuits forms the mechanistic basis the maladaptive changes underlying LID.

> A new species of Cuspicona Dallas, 1851 (Pentatomidae: Pentatominae: Rhynchocorini) is described from eastern Australia. Cuspicona luedkei sp. n. is distinguished from congeners by the strongly produced mesosternal keel extending beneath the head, angulately produced laterotergite VII, spinose humeri, distinctive colour and punctation patterns, and genitalic characters. Adults, eggs, and nymphal instars I–III are described. Diagnostic characters, host associations, behavioural notes, and distribution are also documented. Morphological and mitochondrial evidence (COI, 16S) supports placement of the new species within Cuspicona s. s. > Cancer of unknown primary (CUP) is a heterogeneous group of metastatic malignancies in which the primary site remains unidentified despite appropriate diagnostic evaluation. Historically, most patients with unfavorable CUP have received empirical platinum-based chemotherapy, but recent advances in immune checkpoint inhibition, comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP), tissue-agnostic therapy, and tissue-of-origin prediction are changing the treatment landscape. Contemporary management therefore requires integration rather than simple replacement of empirical therapy. Randomized evidence from CUPISCO supports early CGP with subsequent molecularly guided treatment after disease control with platinum-based induction, while CUP-specific immunotherapy studies and Japanese real-world data demonstrate clinically meaningful activity in selected patients. Conversely, randomized tissue-of-origin-directed trials have produced mixed results, underscoring the need to distinguish diagnostic prediction from proven therapeutic benefit. **Mots-clés détectés :**

  - **case_reports** : case report

**Résumé / abstract :**

> This case report describes a 44-year-old man with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and ineffective secretion clearance despite home use of mechanical insufflation-exsufflation (MI-E). He reported upper airway obstruction, respiratory discomfort and recurrent aerophagia during therapy. Dynamic assessments using transnasal flexible laryngoscopy and videofluoroscopy under different MI-E settings showed that upper airway responses were strongly influenced by inspiratory flow, pressure levels, expiratory time and cervical positioning. Higher inspiratory flow and pressure induced supraglottic closure and airflow diversion to the oesophagus. In contrast, lower inspiratory flow combined with reduced expiratory pressure and shorter expiratory time improved glottic opening, maintained airway patency and enhanced cough mechanics. Spontaneously adopted cervical extension optimized airflow and minimized oesophageal insufflation, whereas neutral alignment impaired cough efficiency. These findings emphasize the importance of individualized MI-E settings and patient-specific biomechanics in optimizing therapy in ALS.

We present the 25-year long-term imaging follow-up of a 39-year-old male with a giant Spetzler–Martin grade V BAVM. Initially diagnosed at age 14 via magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) due to a visual deficit, the complex lesion was managed conservatively owing to prohibitive procedural risks. Twenty-five years later, the patient presented with acute left limb weakness and recurrent adult-onset epilepsy. Current diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) mapping demonstrated chronic ischemic changes in the bilateral frontal lobes and a new acute-to-subacute infarction in the left parietal lobe. Concurrent MRA and MRI demonstrated a massive 13.5 × 6.3 cm nidus with prominent vascular flow voids and deep venous involvement. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Glutamic acid decarboxylase 65 antibody-associated neurological syndrome (GAD65-AINS) is an autoimmune disorder mediated by anti-GAD65 antibodies, with clinical phenotypes including stiff-person spectrum disorders(SPS), limbic encephalitis, cerebellar ataxia, and drug-resistant epilepsy. As the rate-limiting enzyme in GABA synthesis, GAD65 exhibits conformational plasticity, which forms the molecular basis for autoimmune targeting. Genetic susceptibility involves HLA regions (DR3, DR4) and non-HLA immune regulatory genes (e.g., PTPN22, CTLA4), demonstrating a polygenic characteristic. Pathogenic mechanisms involve T-cell-mediated cellular immunity, direct functional interference by antibodies, complement-dependent humoral immune effects, and synergistic enhancement of pathological effects by coexisting antibodies (e.g., anti-CN1A). Diagnosis requires integration of clinical phenotypes, quantitative antibody testing (serum ELISA ≥10,000 IU/mL or RIA ≥20 nmol/L), intrathecal synthesis evidence in CSF, and imaging evaluation. High-titer antibodies are the core diagnostic basis for SPS, but must be interpreted in conjunction with clinical findings.Treatment follows a stratified princip...

> Impairment of quadriceps strength is a frequent and clinically important problem after anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury and reconstruction. This dysfunction reflects muscular, neural, surgical, and rehabilitation-related mechanisms and is not solely attributable to muscle atrophy. Despite restoration of joint stability, quadriceps weakness can persist and contribute to delayed functional recovery and reduced readiness to return to sport. A comprehensive assessment should integrate clinical examination, objective isometric or isokinetic strength testing, rate of force development, functional performance, quality of movement, imaging investigations, and patient-reported and psychological measures. Rehabilitation should be initiated preoperatively and continue postoperatively with a focus on control of effusion and restoration of extension, early quadriceps activation, progressive resistance exercise, appropriate open-chain loading followed by eccentric, plyometric, and sport-specific training. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Wireless implantable neurologgers are emerging as miniature autonomous systems for long-term, untethered neural recording in animal studies. However, the development of wireless systems remains constrained by critical engineering bottlenecks, including neural recording, power supply, and data transmission. This review first systematically summarizes representative commercial neurologgers and state-of-the-art research advances. Then, recent progress in the three engineering areas is reviewed, covering high-performance electrode technologies, efficient wireless power transfer strategies, and advanced communication technologies. The critical trade-offs among energy efficiency, bandwidth, transmission distance, and system complexity are clearly pointed out. Furthermore, the influence of diverse application environments on the system-level design and real-world practicability of neurologgers is analyzed from a new perspective. Finally, the technical challenges and the future directions are discussed to guide the development of fully autonomous wireless implantable neural recording systems for animal studies.

MASLD prevalence in Taiwanese adults is 30%-45%, reaching 60%-70% in individuals with obesity, with similar high prevalence in children and adolescents. **Résumé / abstract :**

> Hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae (hvKp) is an emerging cause of invasive infection, but clinical relevance of a 5-biomarker genotypic definition remains unclear. We analyzed 207 episodes of K. pneumoniae bloodstream infection at a tertiary hospital in Japan during 2022-2024. We defined hvKp by PCR detection of all 5 biomarkers: rmpA, rmpA2, iucA, iroB, and peg-344. Overall, hvKp accounted for 14% (28/207) of episodes. Abscess complications occurred in 61% (17/28) of hvKp episodes and 13% (23/179) of classical K. pneumoniae episodes. hvKp case-patients had longer median hospitalization (28 vs. 14 days) and duration of antimicrobial drug treatment (43 vs. 14 days) than those with classical K. pneumoniae. Most (9/10) sequence type 23 hvKp episodes involved abscesses. Short-read whole-genome sequencing detected CTX-M-type extended-spectrum β-lactamase genes in 11% (3/28) of hvKp isolates, representing 1.4% (3/207) of all K. pneumoniae episodes. The 5-biomarker definition delineated a clinically distinct subgroup, demonstrating its value for genomic surveillance of emerging hvKp.

**Résumé / abstract :**

> Accurate knowledge of microbial etiology is essential for optimizing spinal fusion surgical site infection (SSI) management, yet contemporary national data in the United States, particularly prevalence and factors associated with gram-negative infections, remain poorly understood. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of US data reported to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention National Healthcare Safety Network (2021-2022) to characterize the microbiology of spinal fusion SSI and identify factors associated with gram-negative infection. Among 7,187 cases, gram-negative organisms caused 31.5% (n = 2,265) of SSIs. Older age, female sex, higher body mass index, longer operative times, higher American Society of Anesthesiologists class, lumbar involvement, inpatient surgery, and emergent and trauma surgeries were independently associated with gram-negative infections relative to monomicrobial Staphylococcus aureus infections. Our findings might inform future studies focusing on high-risk cohorts as targets for expanded gram-negative prophylactic regimens. Clinicians can use risk profiles to guide empiric gram-negative antibiotic coverage in treating SSIs.

> Septic arthritis is an important cause of morbidity in calves, and radiographic interpretation may vary between observers, especially when structured scoring systems are used by less experienced readers. This single-center retrospective reader study evaluated whether general-purpose multimodal large language models (LLMs) could support rubric-based radiographic scoring of presumptive septic carpal arthritis in calves. Fifty calves aged 0-3 months with clinical findings consistent with presumptive septic carpal arthritis were included, and one carpal radiograph per case was assessed. Two novice veterinary surgeons and three multimodal LLMs, ChatGPT-5, Gemini-2.5 Pro, and Claude Sonnet-4, independently scored each case using a Constant-based ordinal radiographic scoring framework. Expert consensus served as the operational reference standard. Agreement with the reference was assessed using exact agreement, agreement within one score category, and quadratic weighted kappa. Novice 1 showed the highest concordance, with a mean exact agreement of 55.6%, mean ±1 agreement of 89.8%, and substantial agreement (mean κ w = 0.68; 95% CI, 0.56-0.80). > Esta revisão integrativa sintetizou a evidência publicada entre 2020 e 2026 sobre a prevenção, o diagnóstico e o tratamento do tromboembolismo venoso (TEV) no pós-operatório de cirurgias ortopédicas. A busca na PubMed, em 23 de outubro de 2026, recuperou 582 registros e resultou em 68 estudos, entre os quais 45 revisões, 10 ensaios randomizados, 8 estudos observacionais, 1 diretriz e 4 estudos de outros delineamentos. Na artroplastia, a heparina de baixo peso molecular e os inibidores do fator Xa sustentaram a prevenção, com menos TEV sob anticoagulantes orais diretos do que sob heparina e sangramento dependente do fármaco. > Early return to hospital after discharge is a widely used signal of care quality and a major driver of avoidable cost. This paper reports an explainable machine-learning study that estimates whether a diabetic patient will be readmitted within 30 days, using the public Diabetes 130-US Hospitals data. Keeping only the first encounter of every patient left 69,987 records, of which 5,143 (7.35%) were early readmissions. A single Random Forest classifier with 150 trees and balanced class weights was fitted on 55,989 records and checked on 13,998 unseen ones. It reached 85.1% accuracy, yet precision was 0.174, recall 0.276, F1-score 0.214 and ROC-AUC 0.665, which shows how misleading accuracy becomes under heavy imbalance. Permutation importance ranked the count of earlier inpatient stays first, followed by discharge to skilled nursing and rehabilitation facilities. A 20-feature subset kept almost all of the performance, and a threshold study exposed the precision–recall trade-off that a hospital must manage. The model is best seen as a decision-support aid that complements, and never replaces, clinical judgement.

Methods We retrospectively analyzed 55 adults (mean age 72.1 ± 7.1 years) evaluated for cognitive concerns who had MRI exams including both susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) and gradient echo (GRE) sequences. > Introduction Naturally Occurring Retirement Communities (NORCs) offer a unique opportunity to deliver integrated care within existing housing where older adults already live. In this context, NORCs are defined as high-rise buildings where at least 50 residents and at least 30% of residents are aged 65 and above. This paper presents an implementation case study of the NORC Innovation Centre's (NIC) integrated care model (The UHN NORC Program). Description The UHN NORC Program partners with housing, community, health, and social care providers to enable NORC buildings to adopt community-embedded care. An interprofessional care team collaborates with residents and local organizations to co-design building-level health and wellness programs. Across two Toronto NORCs, the program engaged 60% of residents, with 14% (n = 109) referred for individualized support. Relational care practices that emphasized trust-building, advocacy, and strength-based engagement were key enablers of success, along with the team composition and structure, system partnerships, and community leadership. Despite its recognized importance in developing competent nursing professionals, the application of clinical preceptorship varies considerably across healthcare settings, particularly between public and private hospitals. > Professional nursing standards documents codify what a discipline holds itself accountable to know and act on, and they face increasing political pressure to narrow their equity commitments. In April 2026, the American Association of Colleges of Nursing (AACN) released a revised edition of The Essentials: Core Competencies for Professional Nursing Education, originally approved by member vote in 2021, without a member vote or documented evidence base. This study examined how this revision reconstituted equity-related discourse and what it makes sayable and unsayable in professional nursing education. Using a Foucauldian critical discourse analysis integrated with comparative document analysis. We treated the revision as an instrumental case study and compared both editions line by line. Of 76 document elements compared, 40 were revised, 6 removed, and 27 unchanged; the ten-domain competency architecture remained intact.
